category_summary: **Social** — The section is a single-story week: **hardmaru** (Sakana AI founder) [announces the **Neuroevolution textbook** is finally in print](/?date=2026-09-29&category=social#item-fb3afb75b90d), with a [**free online edition**](/?date=2026-09-29&category=social#item-fb3afb75b90d) at neuroevolutionbook.com and pre-orders open. That anchor milestone post ([fb3afb75b90d], score 68) is the clear newsletter lead — an actual deliverable with a free-access hook — while the remaining four items are companion posts from the same author's thread and rank well behind it. Those thread posts frame the launch through Sakana AI's founding philosophy: the [name and logo inspired by **schools of fish** moving and adapting as one](/?date=2026-09-29&category=social#item-e9377232eb20) ([e9377232eb20]), the thesis that [**intelligence emerges from evolution under constraints**](/?date=2026-09-29&category=social#item-27f8fc53c636) rather than unlimited resources ([27f8fc53c636]), the link between the book's [**open-ended creativity and self-organizing systems**](/?date=2026-09-29&category=social#item-3ef5e718e474) and what Sakana AI builds ([3ef5e718e474]), and a sentimental reflection on why [**neuroevolution**](/?date=2026-09-29&category=social#item-3a8b5d53fb97) convinced him nature builds intelligence through evolution and collective behavior ([3a8b5d53fb97]). Sentiment: community response is respectful but modest — the companion posts drew only a handful of likes and essentially no reposts, reading as a personal victory lap and brand storytelling rather than a viral news moment. Editorial note: since all five items are one coordinated thread by a single high-credibility author, lead with the print-release announcement and treat the philosophy posts as color/quotes rather than standalone stories.
